Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement we need a written confirmation on a few residency questions so our legal and security teams can sign off:

1) For Brightwave's EU tenant (PII from EU patients), can Redwood guarantee that inference requests and logs will remain in the EU under normal operation?

I've attached our DPA redline (brightwave_dpa_redline_v2.pdf). Procurement would like a short statement for their packet that we can include verbatim.

Marco / team — sharing the procurement-friendly language and a couple of notes below. Also attached the current subprocessor export (subprocessor_list_202605.csv).

Procurement paragraph (can be copy/pasted):
"Redwood Inference will process Brightwave Health EU tenant data within the European Union. Under normal operation, inference requests, model execution, and associated logs are routed to and remain on compute located in EU regions. Temporary cross-border processing may occur only in narrowly defined failover scenarios (see below) and is governed by our DPA and audit controls. Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) for EU-region keys; customers may elect to retain key control via integrated KMS providers. A current list of subprocessors and their roles is available and will be provided on execution of the DPA."

Key clarifications and limits:
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and their primary region. We mark subprocessors that may have cross-border access to telemetry; currently none of our primary inference subprocessors require access to raw EU PII.
- DPA redlines: we'll propose narrow language preserving your redlines around residency and notification; legal will send an inline counter by Monday.
- CMK: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/Google Cloud KMS and can scope key policies so the key material never leaves or is exportable outside EU controls when using regional KMS. Note: for on-prem or air-gapped Private deployments we offer HSM integrations.

Marco — technical thread on region pinning and failover behaviors. High level summary first, details below.

Summary: Redwood's "region pinning" routes inference traffic to customer-configured regional pools. For EU-pin: compute, ephemeral caches, and token-level logs are kept in EU regions. Temporary cross-region failover is possible only under explicit conditions and is limited to 30 minutes by default; customers can request a longer window with documented justification and additional controls. Notifications: we provide a webhook + email alert when failover occurs and a post-incident report with timestamps and scope.

Details:
- Pin semantics: customers set a pin policy (strict | best-effort). strict = do not route outside of pinned region except for manual operator intervention (legal/ops-approved) or during a declared catastrophic outage. best-effort = attempt EU first, fallback to nearest region to preserve latency if queues exceed thresholds.
- Failover triggers: (a) complete EU regional capacity depletion for the model variant, (b) scheduled emergency maintenance with multi-hour ETA, (c) region-level network partitioning.
- Max duration: default automatic failover window is up to 30 minutes for auto-burst; if capacity is still unavailable after 30 minutes we keep the request queued and surface a 508-type error to the application unless customer has a longer approved exception.
- Data movement: only request payloads and transient KV caches necessary for completion are routed for the duration of the failover; persistent logs remain subject to EU retention settings unless the customer enables cross-region logging for analytics.
- KMS and encryption: when using Redwood-hosted keys we keep key material in the regional KMS. For CMK, customers can supply a key with a key policy restricting usage to EU-region compute nodes; we can confirm the policy needed.
- Auditability: we generate an exportable failover timeline, per-request routing metadata, and operator approval records for any manual overrides.

Operational ask: Marco, to prepare a short procurement-friendly statement we can add these three bullets to Neha's paragraph to be explicit:
1) Default auto-failover window: 30 minutes (extendable by exception).
2) Notification: webhook + email within 15 minutes of failover initiation.
3) CMK: supported with region-scoped key policy; Redwood will not export key material outside EU region when CMK is used.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to walk procurement/legal through these technical constraints.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
